title: A validator driven by @NotEmpty and @Range

blocks.text: The page's Q5 builds a validation framework in three parts: constraint annotations, a class whose fields carry them, and a processor that reads them through reflection. `@NotEmpty(message)` and `@Range(min, max, message)` are given, with RUNTIME retention and default messages.
Write `Validator.validate(Object obj)`. It checks every field `obj`'s class declares (private ones too) and returns one `Violation(field, message)` per broken rule, sorted by field name:

items: `@NotEmpty`: the value is `null` or a String that is **blank** (only whitespace counts as empty too).
`@Range`: the value is a number outside `min..max`, **both ends inclusive**.

blocks.text: **Every violation is reported**, not only the first. Each uses its annotation's `message()`.

rows: `[age: Invalid age, name: Name is required]`

cases.says: A valid User("Ada", 36) has no violations, and User(null, 36) has one: name, Name is required.
A name of three spaces, or of an em space and a tab, violates @NotEmpty.
Ages 0 and 150 are valid; -1 and 151 violate @Range(min = 0, max = 150).
User("", 200) gets both violations, and a Signup with three broken fields gets all three, sorted by field name.

concepts: A validation framework pairs constraint annotations on fields with a reflective processor that reads each field and its annotation's values and collects every violation.
